original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Certified ceiling beta*t, beta=(27+9*sqrt(2))/7, on every nonnegative permutation-cut combination for t coordinate-three-cycle targets, all finite address dimensions and register counts; sharp real quadratic domination, not the Boolean-cut optimum or word optimum.
scope_change_reason: Take the explicit all-permutation-cut boundary left by PR4968 and PR4974 instead of repeating the GL3 word census or searching a larger register model. The initial fixed-GL3 certificate lifts to all finite dimensions by restriction to each target's embedded subgroup.
bottleneck_link: Side result on a proof method: rules out this entire linear cut relaxation plus final rounding as a way to certify the full 6t tariff for t>=4. It directs any additivity proof to a stronger invariant, without asserting shared paid work or a supplier improvement.
stop_rule: Stop after the exact group-algebra certificate, written uniform implication and bounded checks; no larger word census or Boolean-cut optimization campaign.
evidence: Written cut-cone theorem from exact integer p(L)B=0, verified coefficientwise and independently on all 168 regular basis columns. Exact sharpness vectors, 144 binary paid cross-block checks, four dirty endpoints, all 32768 natural GL4 cuts, rejection controls and normal/optimized replay. No word optimum, Boolean-cut optimum, supplier admission, human or formal-kernel acceptance.
author: Krzysztof Wojt / krzysztofwojt with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. A Luna worker checked recent claims and implemented an independent seven-point-permutation matrix checker; the primary reviewed and integrated it and owns the written proof. Same-session AI assistance, not independent human review. Numerical exploration proposed the identity but is not acceptance evidence.

open_questions.first_step: Supply an explicit feasible cut/weight witness and an independently certified global upper bound, rather than more floating digits.

open_questions.blocked_by: No such additive invariant is supplied; the single-target support floor is not additive.
